statement: Hematopoietic (bone-marrow) stem-cell transplant rebuilds the entire blood and immune system from donor or autologous blood-forming stem cells and is curative for many leukemias, lymphomas, and inherited blood disorders.
effect_size: Standard of care since the 1970s; >1M performed worldwide; curative in many blood malignancies/disorders (carries real GVHD/infection risk).
population: Patients with hematologic malignancies and inherited blood/immune disorders

provenance.primary: E. Donnall Thomas (Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, 1990); decades of RCT + registry data (CIBMTR/EBMT)

confidence_notes: The gold standard of what 'stem-cell therapy' should mean: defined cell type, native target tissue, hard endpoint, decades of evidence. Distinguishes real stem-cell medicine from the predatory clinic tier.

statement: Four transcription factors (OCT4, SOX2, KLF4, MYC) can revert an adult somatic cell to an embryonic-like pluripotent state (induced pluripotent stem cells), proving cell identity is reversible.
effect_size: Foundational; dissolved the one-way-street dogma of differentiation and removed the embryonic-stem-cell ethical bottleneck.

provenance.primary: Takahashi & Yamanaka, Cell 2006; Nobel Prize 2012 (shared with Gurdon)

confidence_notes: Settled as discovery. iPSCs are an unambiguous research/drug-screening tool; iPSC-derived THERAPIES (retina, islets, neurons) are early-stage with real tumorigenicity and immune-rejection hazards.

statement: iPSC-derived cell therapies are in early human trials (macular degeneration, Parkinson's, type-1 diabetes islets, cardiac patches) with promising but preliminary results.
effect_size: Early human pilots (e.g., stem-cell-derived islets restoring insulin); not yet approved products.

provenance.primary: Takahashi 2014 (retinal sheet, Japan); Vertex VX-880 islet program; multiple Phase 1/2 trials

confidence_notes: Legitimate, careful, early. The two governing hazards are teratoma risk from residual pluripotent cells and immune rejection/manufacturing consistency. Correctly moving slowly.

statement: The commercial 'stem-cell clinic' industry sells IV infusions and joint injections (adipose, 'amniotic', umbilical, exosome products) for a long menu of unrelated conditions with no controlled evidence of benefit and documented serious harm.
effect_size: No proven benefit; documented harms include permanent blindness, infection outbreaks, tumors, and death.
population: Cash-pay patients at hundreds of US clinics + medical-tourism sites

provenance.primary: Kuriyan et al. NEJM 2017 (3 patients blinded after intravitreal adipose cells, 10.1056/NEJMoa1609583); FDA injunction vs US Stem Cell Inc. 2019; CDC 2018 cord-blood infection outbreak

confidence_notes: The chapter's sharpest honesty point. Predatory-tier signature: cash-only, long unrelated-condition menu, not in a registered trial, promises regeneration of tissue the cells don't natively build. Burden of proof unmet.

statement: CRISPR-Cas9 is a programmable guide-RNA-directed DNA-cutting system, adapted from a bacterial immune system into a general-purpose gene-editing tool.
effect_size: Foundational editing platform; base-pairing lets a ~20-nt guide RNA address one site in a 3-billion-bp genome.

provenance.primary: Jinek/Doudna & Charpentier, Science 2012; Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2020
provenance.surfaced_via: regenerative-frontier chapter (31) build; tie to 01-foundations DNA fundamentals

confidence_notes: Settled. Rests directly on the DNA/base-pairing fundamentals in 01-foundations.md.

statement: Voretigene neparvovec (Luxturna), an AAV2 vector delivering a working RPE65 gene under the retina, restored functional vision in RPE65-mediated inherited retinal dystrophy and was the first directly-administered gene therapy approved in the US.
effect_size: Improved multi-luminance mobility (functional navigation in dim light); FDA-approved 2017.
population: Patients with biallelic RPE65 retinal dystrophy
confidence_notes: Gene ADDITION (not editing). Durable real success; one of the field's proofs the translation gap can be crossed.

statement: A single intravenous dose of onasemnogene abeparvovec (Zolgensma, AAV9 carrying SMN1) produced motor milestones and survival in type-1 spinal muscular atrophy infants who would otherwise have died.
effect_size: Infants sat/walked who were expected to die; FDA-approved 2019; ~$2.1M list price.

provenance.primary: Mendell et al., NEJM 2017 (single-dose gene-replacement for SMA)

confidence_notes: Dramatic, real. Headline 'most expensive drug' of its era — the access/cost asterisk that recurs across approved gene therapies.

statement: Exagamglogene autotemcel (Casgevy/exa-cel), an ex-vivo CRISPR edit of the patient's own blood stem cells disrupting the BCL11A enhancer to reactivate fetal hemoglobin, freed most severe sickle-cell patients from vaso-occlusive crises and became the first approved CRISPR medicine (FDA, Dec 2023).
effect_size: Majority of treated severe SCD patients free of vaso-occlusive crises; also approved for transfusion-dependent beta-thalassemia; ~$2.2M.
population: Severe sickle-cell disease and transfusion-dependent beta-thalassemia patients

provenance.primary: Frangoul et al., NEJM 2021 (CRISPR-Cas9 for SCD and beta-thalassemia); CLIMB program; FDA approval Dec 2023

confidence_notes: The landmark: first approved gene-EDITING medicine; functional cure for most treated patients. Cruel equity gap: SCD overwhelmingly affects populations least able to access a $2.2M myeloablative therapy.

statement: Approved gene therapies are among the most expensive medicines in history (Zolgensma ~$2.1M, Casgevy ~$2.2M, Hemgenix ~$3.5M, Lenmeldy ~$4.25M), and the populations most affected by some target diseases are least able to access them.
effect_size: Per-patient prices $2M-$4.25M; rare-disease economics + per-patient manufacturing limit scale and global reach.
population: Patients with approved gene-therapy indications worldwide

provenance.primary: FDA approvals + manufacturer list prices (Novartis, Vertex/CRISPR Tx, CSL Behring, Orchard); Lenmeldy 2024 most-expensive-drug reporting

confidence_notes: 'Cured in principle' does heavy lifting for most of the world's patients. Real, unsolved equity problem, not a footnote.

statement: Heritable human germline genome editing crosses the field's ethical bright line; the one documented case (He Jiankui's 2018 CRISPR-edited twins) was scientifically reckless, addressed no unmet need, and was condemned worldwide and criminally prosecuted.
effect_size: Edits were imprecise/mosaic, CCR5-disruption HIV rationale was unjustified, consent/oversight violated; He convicted/imprisoned in China (2019); global moratorium calls followed.
population: Two edited human embryos ('Lulu and Nana')

provenance.primary: He Jiankui 2018 announcement; international scientific condemnation; Chinese court conviction 2019

confidence_notes: Distinct from somatic editing (which is not inherited and underlies all approved gene therapies). Heritable germline editing is currently prohibited/unfunded across essentially all serious jurisdictions; consensus: not safe or justified.

statement: Cyclic partial (Yamanaka-factor) reprogramming reverses cellular aging hallmarks and, in mice, extends lifespan (progeroid) and restores vision (aged/glaucomatous) without erasing cell identity.
effect_size: Lifespan extension in progeroid mice (Ocampo); vision restoration in aged mice (Lu/Sinclair). No human efficacy data.
canon_link: bucket-canon/05-biophysics/ (epigenetic information, the 'information theory of aging')
confidence_notes: ANIMAL-tier only. The Altos (~$3B)/Retro/NewLimit bet. Funding is provenance, not evidence (LABS.md rule). No human has been age-reversed by reprogramming.

statement: The central, non-theoretical hazard of cellular reprogramming is cancer: the factors are reprogramming factors, MYC is an oncogene, and incomplete/excessive reprogramming can cause teratomas and loss of cell identity.
effect_size: Whole research problem is dosing rejuvenation without tipping into oncogenesis; this safety margin is unproven in humans.

provenance.primary: Reprogramming-toxicity literature; rationale for OSK (dropping MYC) in Lu/Sinclair 2020

confidence_notes: Also: epigenetic-clock 'rejuvenation' is a surrogate, not an outcome. Moving a Horvath/PhenoAge reading is not extending healthy human life.

statement: Gene-edited pig organs were transplanted into humans for the first time in 2021-2022 (kidneys; a heart into David Bennett Sr., Jan 2022), but all earliest recipients died within weeks to months.
effect_size: First pig-to-human heart recipient survived ~2 months (porcine CMV + rejection implicated); historic firsts, none durable.
population: Brain-dead and compassionate-use living recipients (n very small)

provenance.primary: Griffith et al., NEJM 2022 (genetically modified porcine-to-human cardiac xenotransplantation); NYU/UAB/MGH pig-kidney cases

confidence_notes: Real, historic, very early. Cross-species rejection, latent animal viruses, and long-term function remain unsolved. Not a clinical option; experimental compassionate-use only.

statement: 3D bioprinting can produce flat/thin tissue constructs (pre-clinical) but not solid vascularized organs; organoids are a valuable research/drug-screening tool, not a transplantable product.
effect_size: Vascularizing thick tissue is the unsolved bottleneck for printed solid organs (years-to-decades). Organoids are mm-scale, unvascularized, incomplete.

provenance.primary: Tissue-engineering and organoid literature (Lancaster/Knoblich organoid reviews; bioprinting vascularization reviews)

confidence_notes: 'We grew a brain organoid' is not 'we can replace a brain' — exactly the mechanism-to-outcome laundering SCHEMA.md forbids.

statement: Intra-articular platelet-rich plasma is no better than saline placebo for pain or cartilage volume in knee osteoarthritis in the best-designed trial, despite heavy marketing as regenerative healing.
effect_size: RESTORE RCT: no significant benefit vs placebo for pain or medial tibial cartilage volume at 12 months.

provenance.primary: Bennell et al., JAMA 2021 (RESTORE randomized clinical trial)

confidence_notes: Meta-analyses heterogeneous and dominated by small high-bias trials; rigorous blinding shrinks effect toward placebo. PRP is non-standardized (a dozen preparations). Possible modest signal in lateral epicondylitis/some tendinopathies; inconsistent. Low harm, largely unproven value.

statement: Commercial 'regenerative' joint injections (adipose SVF, bone-marrow aspirate concentrate, amniotic and exosome products) have weak, small, inconsistent evidence; many 'amniotic stem-cell' products contain no living stem cells and the FDA has acted against marketers.
effect_size: No established efficacy for OA/tendon injury; products unstandardized and frequently mislabeled.

provenance.primary: FDA enforcement actions + product-characterization studies showing absent viable cells

confidence_notes: Joint-injection cousins of the §2.3 clinic tier. Sold far ahead of evidence.

statement: Prolotherapy (hypertonic dextrose injection) has a mixed evidence base with some modest-benefit RCT signals in knee osteoarthritis and chronic lateral epicondylitis, but small heterogeneous trials and no high-quality confirmation.
effect_size: Possible modest niche effect; not established; not a regenerative cure.
population: Knee OA and chronic lateral epicondylitis patients

provenance.primary: Prolotherapy RCTs (e.g., Rabago knee-OA dextrose trials) + systematic reviews noting heterogeneity/bias

confidence_notes: Slightly better-than-PRP but still mixed/low-quality base. For joint/tendon pain the strongest-evidence interventions remain load-management and progressive exercise.

statement: The well-capitalized 'cure aging' industry reliably extends mouse lifespan but has produced thin human clinical output; Calico (~$2.5B, 10+ yrs) shows minimal translation and Unity's lead senolytic UBX0101 failed its first human knee-OA trial.
effect_size: Mouse lifespan extension is reproducible; human hard-endpoint translation is largely absent. Human trials mostly repurposed drugs vs surrogate endpoints.
population: Industry programs (Altos, Calico, Retro, NewLimit, Unity, BioAge, Gero)

provenance.primary: LABS.md industry synthesis; Unity UBX0101 Phase 2 failure (2020); Loyal FDA RXE for canine aging drug (2023); TAME trial design

confidence_notes: Mice are short-lived/inbred/lab-housed/cancer-prone in ways that flatter interventions. The mouse result is the beginning of the question, not the answer. Loyal's canine RXE is the closest a regulator has come to treating aging itself as an indication.
